metadata.headline: Why can multiple sellers share one Amazon product page?

platform_lesson.title: The catalog is platform infrastructure
platform_lesson.text: Amazon separates the customer-facing product page from each Seller's individual offer. One product detail page can contain competing offers from multiple Sellers, while Amazon controls how product information is presented and which eligible offer becomes the Featured Offer. Independent Sellers therefore contribute inventory, price and fulfillment without owning the main catalog surface through which customers compare supply. This lets Amazon centralize discovery, comparison and trust while keeping much of the inventory decentralized. The platform lesson is that a marketplace can control how supply competes by controlling the catalog, even when it does not own the underlying inventory.

core_value_unit.explanation: The Seller Offer is the Provider-specific Core Value Unit in this Amazon Marketplace case. Amazon's own documentation distinguishes the shared product detail page from the offers attached to it: several Sellers can offer the same product with different prices, condition and fulfillment. The source presentation called this a 'product listing'; this case uses 'Seller Offer' to reflect Amazon's current catalog architecture more precisely.

metrics.note: U.S.-based independent sellers sold more than 4.6 billion items in Amazon's store in 2025. This is annual throughput through seller offers, not the number of live offers.

actor.explanation: Shoppers are the demand side of the marketplace: customers who search Amazon's shared catalog and choose among Amazon and third-party offers.

metrics.note: Amazon states that more than 200 million paid Prime members exist globally. This is a broad demand-side scale proxy: not every Prime member buys from Marketplace Sellers, and non-Prime customers also shop on Amazon.

job.explanation: Shoppers want to find and purchase products without having to evaluate every Seller or fulfillment option from scratch.

gain.explanation: The marketplace combines broad selection with Amazon's discovery, checkout and delivery experience.

pain.explanation: Multiple Sellers can improve choice but also create uncertainty around price, condition, fulfillment, Seller quality and which offer to choose.

transaction.explanation: The Shopper selects an offer, places the order and pays through Amazon's checkout rather than sending payment directly to the Seller.

filter.explanation: Access depends on market availability, payment capability, fraud controls and product-specific restrictions.

access_channel.explanation: Shoppers enter through Amazon's website, Shopping app and other Amazon shopping surfaces.

activities.explanation: Shoppers search the catalog, compare products and Seller offers, order, track, return and review.

resources.explanation: Shoppers contribute purchasing power, delivery information, account data, preferences and behavioral signals.

actor.explanation: Independent Sellers are the Provider side because they contribute third-party inventory and commercial offers. Amazon's own first-party retail inventory is deliberately outside this Provider role; this PBMC isolates the Marketplace subsystem.

metrics.note: In Q2 2026, Seller units were 61% of worldwide paid units, excluding Whole Foods Market. This measures the share of units sold by Sellers, not the number of active Seller accounts.
More than 75,000 independent Sellers surpassed $1 million in Amazon-store sales in 2025. This is a high-volume Seller cohort, not the total Seller population.

job.explanation: Independent Sellers want to convert inventory into sales by reaching Amazon's large customer base.

gain.explanation: Sellers gain customer reach, trust infrastructure, data, advertising options and optional fulfillment capabilities.

pain.explanation: Sellers face referral and optional service fees, competition from other offers, Featured Offer pressure and dependence on Amazon's marketplace rules.

transaction.explanation: The Seller contributes an offer with price, inventory, condition and fulfillment attributes, then supplies the product when that offer wins the order.

filter.explanation: Amazon verifies Seller identity and requires compliance with product, category, legal and marketplace policies.

access_channel.explanation: Sellers manage offers and operations through Seller Central, the Seller app and supported APIs.

activities.explanation: Sellers create or match products, maintain offers, manage inventory and pricing, advertise, fulfill orders and handle service obligations.

resources.explanation: Sellers contribute inventory, pricing, product and offer data, images, compliance information and fulfillment capacity.

actor.explanation: This Partner role is intentionally narrower than the source presentation's broad mix of logistics, payments and cloud firms. It covers Amazon-vetted third-party software and service providers whose complementary value is delivered directly to Sellers through the Selling Partner Appstore and Service Provider Network.

metrics.note: Amazon's Selling Partner Appstore developer page states that the Appstore has 2,500+ applications. This measures the software-partner subset, not every Service Provider Network firm.
Amazon states that 1.4 million+ Sellers use apps in the Selling Partner Appstore ecosystem. This measures Sellers reached by the software-partner layer, not Partner companies.

job.explanation: Seller Solution Partners help independent Sellers automate or outsource specialist tasks required to operate and grow on Amazon.

gain.explanation: Partners gain access to a large Seller customer base and can monetize software subscriptions or specialist services.

pain.explanation: Partners depend on Amazon APIs, policy compliance, data security and continued marketplace access.

transaction.explanation: Sellers purchase software or specialist services from Partners and provide the data or permissions needed to perform those services.

filter.explanation: Amazon reviews software partners and vets Service Provider Network participants, monitors performance and requires compliance with platform standards.

access_channel.explanation: Partners reach Sellers through the Selling Partner Appstore, Service Provider Network and integrations with Seller Central.

activities.explanation: Partners build apps or deliver specialist services such as advertising optimization, compliance, taxes, cataloging, shipping and operational support.

resources.explanation: Partners contribute applications, APIs, specialist staff, operational know-how and Seller-facing support.

actor.explanation: Amazon owns and governs the Marketplace subsystem inside its broader store. It controls the shared catalog, discovery surfaces, checkout and rules while also operating its own first-party retail business.

metrics.note: Amazon reported $46.780 billion of Third-party seller services net sales in Q2 2026. Amazon defines this category as commissions plus related fulfillment and shipping fees and other third-party Seller services; it is not the gross merchandise value of third-party products.

job.explanation: Amazon must coordinate decentralized third-party supply inside a customer experience that still feels like one coherent store.

gain.explanation: More Seller supply increases selection and transaction density while generating commissions and optional Seller-service revenue.

pain.explanation: Amazon must manage counterfeit risk, unsafe products, poor Seller performance and regulatory scrutiny while also competing as a first-party retailer inside the wider store.

transaction.explanation: Amazon structures discovery, selects how competing offers are displayed, processes the order and payment, and coordinates Seller proceeds.

governance.explanation: Amazon controls the shared product catalog, Seller eligibility, Featured Offer logic, product rules, reviews and customer-protection mechanisms.

promotion_channel.explanation: Amazon attracts and retains demand through its store, search, Prime, advertising, promotions and the broader Amazon brand.

activities.explanation: Amazon runs catalog matching, search and ranking, Featured Offer selection, checkout, payment coordination, trust and safety, and Seller tooling.

resources.explanation: The shared catalog, customer demand, transaction data, brand, marketplace technology, payments and logistics capabilities are central resources.

current.explanation: The Shopper selects an offer and sends the order and payment through Amazon's checkout.
Amazon provides the shared product catalog, offer comparison, checkout and protections such as the A-to-z Guarantee for eligible third-party purchases.
Independent Sellers provide offer data and pay selling and optional service fees to Amazon.
Amazon exposes Seller offers to customer demand and sends Seller proceeds after the order and applicable deductions.
The independent Seller supplies the purchased product, either through its own fulfillment or using Amazon fulfillment infrastructure.
Buyer feedback and Seller feedback create reputation and demand signals that affect future marketplace transactions.
Sellers pay third-party Solution Partners and authorize the business or marketplace data required for their chosen software or service.
Seller Solution Partners return software, automation or specialist operating services directly to the Seller.
Amazon provides qualified Partners with Selling Partner APIs, Appstore or SPN access and exposure to the Seller ecosystem.
Partners extend the Marketplace ecosystem with third-party applications and services that Amazon can make discoverable to Sellers.

metrics.note: Q2 2026 Third-party seller services net sales; commissions, related fulfillment/shipping fees and other Seller services.
Global paid Prime members; broad demand proxy, not Marketplace-only active Buyers.
Q2 2026 worldwide Seller unit mix excluding Whole Foods Market.
Selling Partner Appstore software-partner scale; not all service partners.
Items sold by U.S.-based independent Sellers in 2025; throughput, not live Seller Offers.
